about: The registry of FEATURE shorts (make_feature_story.py; SKILL.md, section Feature shorts). One entry = one feature of the site, the one question it answers and the real card that answers it. Schema /2 (owner verdict 2026-11-10: "they arent good, only the last one show the visuals correctly as it shown on website"): the payoff is the site's card WHOLE, captured as one strip of the page at phone width (`site`), shown large in one window, scrolled like a thumb when it is taller than the stage, with the key outlined where it stands. Fragment cards, crops and 6x key captures are refused. Lines never hold a number, a ticker or a name: those are {slots}, read from the capture's text on the render day. A capitalised word in the middle of a line must be listed in proper_words (a person or a company is never typed).

features.title: Congress trades (market in pictures)
features.post_note: The card counts the stock trades members of Congress disclosed in the site's disclosure window; it shows no dates, so do not add a period in the post text unless you read it on the page. Counts, not dollars. The card's "Most traded" row shows tickers with their small company logos, as the site draws it.
features.about_page: /market is a permanent redirect to the home page's Market section (/#market): the capture asks for /market and the browser ends on /#market. The card is far below the page header, so the header is not in the strip (the brand pill carries the brand).
refuse_if: No stock trades by members of Congress were disclosed

checks.why: the story is a day the card shows more sells than buys

features.title: Insider trades (market in pictures)
features.post_note: Open-market buys and sales by company officers and directors of their own company's stock; the card says 30-day totals. The rows show tickers with their small company logos, as the site draws it.
features.about_page: /market is a permanent redirect to the home page's Market section (/#market). The card is far below the page header, so the header is not in the strip.

checks.why: the story is a day the card shows more sold than bought

features.title: Portfolio concentration (sample portfolio)
features.post_note: The numbers are the site's read-only sample portfolio: say so in the post text. Same page as the portfolio short: do not post the two close together.
features.about_page: The strip is the Portfolio Concentration card from its title to the bottom of its two-ring donut (the card's box for the gates ends there: the lists below it are the portfolio short's scroll). The card starts a screen below the page header, so the header is not in the strip.

values.rx: (?P<share>\d+(?:\.\d+)?%) of your money is in (?P<n>\d+) chip companies\.

checks.why: the story is about a portfolio the page calls Concentrated
the hook needs several chip companies

features.title: Portfolio page (sample portfolio)
features.post_note: The numbers are the site's read-only sample portfolio (the screen says READ-ONLY SAMPLE): say so in the post text. Same page as the concentration short: do not post the two close together.
features.about_page: The strip is the page from its header down to the end of LARGEST HOLDINGS: one continuous scroll (value header, the concentration card and its donut, SECTORS, BIGGEST INDUSTRY GROUPS, LARGEST HOLDINGS), then back up to the sector row that is the key.

values.rx: (?P<sector>[A-Z][A-Za-z &]+) is (?P<pct>\d+(?:\.\d+)?%) of your money\. In the S&P 500 it's (?P<bench>\d+(?:\.\d+)?%)\.

checks.why: the story is about one sector holding a large share of the money

features.title: Market breadth (market in pictures)
features.post_note: A dated fact: the card and the voice name the session's weekday. Post it before the next US session closes, or capture and render it again; never later.
features.answers: How much of the market actually moved with the headline?
features.about_page: /market is a permanent redirect to the home page's Market section (/#market): the capture asks for /market and the browser ends on /#market. The card is far below the page header, so the header is not in the strip.

a breadth count of a few stocks is a page that did not load its data
